articles.title: Falcons safety ranked among top NFL free agents in 2027
articles.summary: Jessie Bates III deserves extension after 3 stellar years in Atlanta.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons have one of the most talented secondaries in the NFL, and they added more fuel to the fire by drafting cornerback Avieon Terrell in the second round. With nickel Billy Bowman Jr. on the verge of returning and safety Xavier Watts coming off of a five-interception rookie season, there's a lot to like on the back end.

While these young players appear to have bright futures, Jessie Bates III has been playing elite football for the Falcons ever since signing in Atlanta as a free agent in 2023. The Pro Bowl safety has recorded 13 interceptions, 27 passes defended and three touchdowns over the last three seasons.

Bates is set to be a free agent next offseason, and would likely have no shortage of suitors if he hits the open market. NFL.com ranked Atlanta's ballhawk among the top 25 free agents in 2027. Bates landed at No. 23 on the list.

"In a thin year for free-agent safeties, Bates still brings veteran know-how," wrote NFL.com's Gregg Rosenthal .

General manager Ian Cunningham has gotten four big extensions done thus far, but there seems to be less urgency when it comes to re-signing Bates. If the Falcons want to retain players who stay on the field and produce, Bates deserves to be rewarded with at least a short-term extension.

The former Cincinnati Bengals standout hasn't missed a game since coming to Atlanta. At 29 years old, Bates is still playing great football. He earned a second-team All-Pro nod in 2025, which was his first such honor since 2020.

The Falcons have the money, and with key players locked up, it's time to pay Bates what he deserves.

articles.title: Man City Starting XI vs Coventry City Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
articles.summary: Man City Predicted XI vs Coventry: Enzo Fernandez Ready for Etihad DebutManchester City have spent heavily, and now Enzo Maresca has to make the signings fit...
articles.body:
Man City Predicted XI vs Coventry: Enzo Fernandez Ready for Etihad Debut

Manchester City have spent heavily, and now Enzo Maresca has to make the signings fit. That is the job. No excuses, no hiding place. After a Deadline Day outlay that brought Enzo Fernandez, Iliman Ndiaye and Ayyoub Bouaddi through the door, City head into the Coventry game with serious depth and a few awkward decisions.

Fernandez is the headline act. The midfielder arrived for a British transfer record-equalling £125m and is expected to go straight into the starting side. Ndiaye, signed for up to £65m, may have to wait, while Bouaddi, who cost £86m, also looks more likely to begin on the bench. When clubs spend like this, places disappear quickly.

The first obvious consequence is in midfield. Marc Guehi's brief spell as a defensive midfielder looks over. It was a useful experiment, little more. With Fernandez available, City can restore some order in the centre of the pitch, with Elliot Anderson likely to provide balance alongside him.

That also increases the pressure on the attacking midfield spots. Rayan Cherki has started the season well, Phil Foden remains a major talent, and neither can assume anything. Competition is what City wanted, and now they have it.

At the back, Abdukodir Khusanov is set to start on the right side of defence, with Ruben Dias and Guehi likely to form the central pairing. Josko Gvardiol should continue on the left. It looks more stable than the constant reshuffling seen early in the campaign, and that matters against a Coventry side who will look for any opening.

Matheus Nunes remains a fitness doubt, while Jeremy Doku is still sidelined with the calf injury suffered against Arsenal in the Community Shield.

Predicted Man City XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Semenyo, Cherki, Foden; Haaland.

The match kicks off at 3pm BST on Saturday, September 2, 2026, at the Etihad Stadium. City have spent enough. Now they need coherence, authority and three points.

articles.title: Chicago Sky owner’s ruthless response to Enes Kanter’s lawsuit is going viral
articles.summary: Former NBA star Enes Kanter Freedom receives a response after suing the Chicago Sky. Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected and indefinitely banned from the Wintrus...
articles.body:
Former NBA star Enes Kanter Freedom receives a response after suing the Chicago Sky.

Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected and indefinitely banned from the Wintrust Arena on August 23, 2026, due to a confrontation with Chicago Sky's Natasha Cloud.

Kanter was also wearing a T-Shirt with 'Woman noun. Adult human female' text, which led to Cloud engaging in a verbal battle with the controversial basketball star.

Following the altercation, Kanter sued the Sky for allegedly violating his First Amendment free speech rights.

Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter responds to Enes Kanter's lawsuit

Kanter's battle with the Sky took another turn when the team's principal owner, Michael Alter, released a statement calling out the 34-year-old's lawsuit.

"We received word that the entity owning the Chicago Sky is being sued by Mr. Enes Kanter Freedom for allegedly violating his First Amendment rights. This lawsuit is meritless and frivolous.

"Freedom's claim that he was removed from Wintrust Arena due to his speech is false," Alter said in his statement, per Kareem Copeland on X .

Alter added, "As his own complaint acknowledges, he wore the shirt in question for multiple hours without any contact with security.

"Security removed Freedom only after he violated fan code of conduct by rising from his seat, gesturing at a player, and stepping toward the court. Freedom was removed for his conduct, not his speech. We look forward to the truth prevailing in court."

The Sky owner essentially called Kanter Freedom's lawsuit baseless as the team's legal counsel prepares to challenge it in court.

Meanwhile, Kanter Freedom is focused on his next controversy after suggesting he should be made the WNBA's next commissioner after Cathy Engelbert announced her retirement from the position at the end of the season.

articles.title: Will CSU and Wyoming rivalry continue through conference realignment?
articles.summary: When do Wyoming and CSU football play again in the Border War? A look at all the future scheduled matchups between the rivals.
articles.body:
The 2026 Border War is the earliest football meeting in the long history between Colorado State and Wyoming .

The teams play Sept. 5 at Canvas Stadium to open the 2026 season. The matchup happens so early due to conference realignment.

A conference has always been shared by the rivals. Until now. CSU is now in the Pac-12 and Wyoming is in the Mountain West. Realignment has seen many rivalries be shelved across college football, but the Border War will continue with a contract signed through the mid 2030s.

The biggest question right now is 2027. The teams don't currently have a game lined up for next season, but the schools said they're working on it in a Sept. 2 release announcing matchups in other sports .

"The two schools are working together to continue the football series in 2027," the release said.

Here are all the future Border War matchups in football currently set by contract.
